claim: During a constant stimulus and percept, face-patch activity alternates about 15 times per second between conscious and suppressed micro-epochs
quote: the brain rapidly alternates, about 15 times per second, between conscious and suppressed micro-epochs

claim: Analyses used 300-1000 ms after the flash, when humans reported the flashed stimulus dominating
quote: For all subsequent analyses, we focus on the period 300 to 1000 ms after the flash, where the flashed stimulus dominated perception and the priming stimulus was suppressed.

claim: Neuropixels probes targeted face patches ML and AM in IT and orbitofrontal (PO) and ventrolateral (PVL) prefrontal regions
quote: face patches ML and AM in inferotemporal cortex, and the orbitofrontal (PO) and ventrolateral (PVL) regions of prefrontal cortex

claim: Modulation during binocular flash suppression was much weaker than during unambiguous alternation, slope 0.23
quote: with nearly all points falling below the identity diagonal (slope = 0.23)

claim: 1500 faces were presented in flash suppression to map each cell's feature code
quote: To precisely map the feature code of each cell, we presented 1500 faces in flash suppression.

claim: After the flash the LLR-decoded population alternated between states, occupying state 1 and state 2 about equally
quote: the population rapidly alternated between the two states, and state 1 and state 2 were occupied about equally

claim: The LLR signal autocorrelation decayed with a 67 ms time constant; time-shuffled data decayed within one bin
quote: It decayed with a time constant of 67 ms, whereas the same signal computed after shuffling time points decayed within a single bin

claim: Reconstructions from state 1 resembled the conscious face; from state 2 the suppressed face
quote: Strikingly, reconstructions computed from activity during state 1 closely resembled the conscious face, whereas reconstructions computed from state 2 closely resembled the suppressed face

claim: A time-averaged null model without state segmentation reconstructed the average of the two faces
quote: produced reconstructions that matched neither the conscious nor the suppressed face, but rather their average

claim: In state 1, conscious-face reconstruction exceeded 80% explained variance for some features, near the >90% priming upper bound
quote: During state 1, prediction of the consciously perceived face reached over 80% explained variance for some features.

claim: In state 2, suppressed-face explained variance was high but slightly lower than the conscious face in state 1
quote: explained variance for the suppressed stimulus was now high, albeit slightly lower than for the conscious face during state 1

claim: Single-trial decoding from binocular-period average activity was about equal for conscious and suppressed stimuli (40% vs 34%)
quote: decoding using average activity during the binocular condition was about equal for the conscious and suppressed stimuli (40% and 34%, respectively)

claim: Restricted to state 1, conscious stimulus decoding was over 61% vs 4% for suppressed
quote: During state 1, on the other hand, the conscious stimulus was decoded far more accurately than the suppressed stimulus (over 61% versus 4%;

claim: Using the same data to define states and evaluate them creates circular conditioning bias that inflates separation
quote: the circular re-use of the same data samples allows each neuron’s independent spiking fluctuations to influence both state assignment and its subsequent state-conditioned response

claim: A two-state model gave higher likelihood than the best single-state model in all 19 sessions
quote: The two-state model assigned higher likelihood to the observed population activity than the best single-state model for all 19 sessions

claim: Held-out half of neurons reconstructed the conscious face in state 1 and suppressed in state 2 as defined by the other half
quote: the held-out population reconstructed the conscious face during epochs classified as state 1 by the other half of the neurons, and the suppressed face during epochs classified as state 2

claim: Leave-one-neuron-out raised EV only ~2 points over split-half, so accuracy was not limited by neuron count
quote: showing that state inference and reconstruction accuracy were not limited by neuron count

claim: Restricting split-half analysis to high-confidence time points raised EV by 10 percentage points
quote: restricting the split-half analysis to high-confidence time points increased explained variance by 10 percentage points

claim: Subsampling equal state samples per trial kept reconstructions robust, ruling out between-trial differences
quote: Thus, the separation between conscious and suppressed representations cannot be explained by different stimuli being represented on different trials

claim: With randomly shuffled templates, reconstructions did not resemble the templates and explained variance was largely below zero
quote: reconstructions obtained with randomly re-assigned templates did not resemble the templates, and their explained variance was largely below zero

claim: Single cells ramped along their preferred axis with the conscious face in state 1 and the suppressed face in state 2
quote: In individual cells, the ramp appeared for the conscious face during state 1 and for the suppressed face during state 2

claim: Conscious-face tuning gain in state 1 exceeded suppressed-face gain in state 2, mean ratio 1.21
quote: mean ratio between conscious and suppressed tuning gain = 1.21

claim: Across cells, conscious-face gain in state 1 correlated strongly with suppressed-face gain in state 2 (r = 0.90): same neurons encode both
quote: indicating that the same neurons encoded both faces

claim: Mean firing rate was weakly but significantly higher in state 2
quote: a small mean-rate offset (higher in state 2)

claim: A linear decoder distinguished state-1 from state-2 responses with 66% accuracy
quote: A linear decoder distinguished state-1 from state-2 responses with 66% accuracy

claim: In state 1, binocular modulation matched unambiguous modulation, slope 0.93
quote: Modulation indices clustered around the diagonal (slope = 0.93)

claim: In state 2, modulation was anticorrelated with unambiguous modulation, slope -0.76
quote: Modulation indices clustered around the antidiagonal (slope = -0.76)

claim: After equalising tuning gain across states and weighting by occupancy, the residual positive correlation disappeared
quote: after this correction the residual positive correlation disappeared

claim: With an HMM at the 5 ms peak-likelihood bin, median dwell times were 64 ms (state 1) and 59 ms (state 2)
quote: median dwell times for state 1 and state 2 were very similar, 64 ms and 59 ms, respectively

claim: In a four-state On/Off decoder, the conscious/suppressed partition agreed with a firing-rate partition no better than chance
quote: the conscious/suppressed partition agreed with a partition by total firing rate (separating bins into higher/lower than median firing rate) no better than chance

claim: Conscious/suppressed states from the four-state model agreed 80% with the original two-state model
quote: agreed closely with those from the original two-state model (Fig. 2a; 80% agreement)

claim: Inferring states in one face patch and predicting features in the other gave weak evidence for cross-patch coordination
quote: However, our results do not provide strong evidence for coordination across patches in generating conscious and suppressed micro-epochs.

claim: In the model-by-test battery, only the two-state model reproduced every signature; each alternative failed at least three tests
quote: each alternative failed at least three of the tests

claim: Two-state, averaging and uncoordinated models all passed circular state-resolved reconstruction above chance
quote: The two-state, averaging, and uncoordinated models could all reconstruct the conscious face in inferred state 1 and the suppressed face in inferred state 2 above chance using circular analysis

claim: At matched dwell (~80 ms) real data beat the averaging model by 8.2% explained variance
quote: real data yielded significantly better reconstructions than the averaging model (Δ = 8.2% explained variance at ~80 ms dwell

claim: Split-half reconstruction held for real data and the two-state model but collapsed for averaging and uncoordinated models
quote: reconstruction held in the real data and the two-state model but collapsed for the averaging and uncoordinated models

claim: For averaging and uncoordinated models a single-state HMM fit held-out data better than two states
quote: For the averaging and uncoordinated models, by contrast, a single state fit better than two

claim: In PFC, best-possible EV from priming was below 80% vs over 90% in IT, and under 30% for shape features
quote: the best possible explained variance, reconstructing faces from priming responses, was below 80%, compared to over 90% for inferotemporal cortex

claim: In PFC, states inferred from one half reconstructed faces from the held-out half with persistent state-dependent separation
quote: when the states were inferred from one half of the prefrontal population and the faces reconstructed from the held-out half, the state-dependent separation persisted

claim: PFC modulation slopes were 0.32 averaged, 0.91 in state 1 and -0.52 in state 2
quote: During state 1, however, modulation resembled the conscious stimulus (slope = 0.91) and during state 2 modulation resembled the suppressed stimulus (slope = -0.52)

claim: Representational switches occur over an order of magnitude faster (15 Hz) than perceptual switches (~0.5 Hz)
quote: These representational switches in neural activity happen over an order of magnitude faster (15 Hz) than perceptual switches (~0.5 Hz)

claim: Lower cross-validated EV in real data than the ideal simulation may reflect non-instantaneous transitions in real populations
quote: may partly reflect the fact that transitions in biological neural populations are unlikely to be instantaneous
